subtopic: AOTInductor runtime behavior on shape mismatch
learningObjective: Understand how AOTInductor artifacts behave at runtime with respect to dynamic shapes and shape mismatch.
stem: An AOTInductor artifact was produced from an ExportedProgram with sequence dim declared dynamic via `Dim("seq", min=1, max=8192)`. Which statements about its runtime behavior are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Loading and running the artifact does not re-invoke torch.compile; the shared library already contains compiled kernels and a small runtime wrapper.
Calling the artifact with a sequence length outside the declared `[1, 8192]` range is expected to raise a shape-constraint error at runtime rather than to trigger recompilation.

Calling the artifact with a sequence length inside the declared range but with a different device (e.g., CPU when the artifact was compiled for CUDA) transparently migrates execution to the runtime device with a small performance penalty.
AOTInductor artifacts require dimensions not declared dynamic to match the export-time example exactly at runtime.

explanation: A, B, D are correct: the artifact does not re-invoke torch.compile at load time; violations of declared shape constraints raise runtime errors (not recompiles, since the artifact was compiled AOT); and dims not declared dynamic are treated as static and must match the export-time example. C is wrong: the artifact targets the hardware present at compile time; running on a different device does not transparently migrate.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: AOTInductor's model is static after compile, so constraint violations are errors.

assumptions: The user supplied the necessary Dim constraints at export time; other dims stay static.
nonImplications: Does not imply AOTInductor cannot serve dynamic-batch scenarios; users must declare dynamic dims explicitly.
Does not imply the compile-time target must match every deployment detail (some minor toolchain versions are fine).
